The coefficients  $ \hat{\phi}_{0}, \hat{\phi}_{1}, \ldots, \hat{\phi}_{k-1} $ of the root function (2.7) will be called generalized Jordan vectors. Recall that, in the special case where the operator-valued function  $ Q(z) $ is a matrix polynomial, the corresponding vectors are called generalized eigenvectors or Jordan vectors; see [6, p. 24], [2].

Remark 2.1. If the function  $ \Psi(z) $ is a pole cancellation function of  $ Q(z) $ at  $ \beta $ of order  $ k \in \mathbb{N} $,  $ k < m $, then the coefficients  $ \Psi_k, \ldots, \Psi_m $ must satisfy conditions (2.2) and (2.3). These conditions will therefore be used to determine the coefficients.
